plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with vivid bracts that are often mistaken for petals, surrounding small yellow true flowers called cyathia. In its native range it can grow up to 4 meters tall, and it blooms in response to the long nights of late autumn and winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; widely cultivated worldwide as a holiday plant
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants that need at least 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness for around 8 weeks to develop their colored bracts. The Aztecs used the plant to make a reddish dye and called it cuetlaxochitl.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. In mild climates it blooms through the cool months, brightening gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring (December to March, with early cultivars flowering in December)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China; grown in the southeastern United States, western Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Camellia oil has been used in Japan for centuries as a hair and skin treatment and for cooking.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with large trumpet-shaped flowers borne on tall, sturdy stems. In the Southern Hemisphere, garden amaryllis bloom naturally in early summer, and forced bulbs in the north bloom indoors in winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere in winter
plants.location: Native to tropical Americas and the Caribbean; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: A single amaryllis bulb can send up several flower stalks, and some large bulbs can produce flowers up to 25 cm across. Many people mistakenly call it amaryllis, but the true Amaryllis genus is a separate South African group.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers on tall stems. It thrives in the warm summer weather of the Southern Hemisphere in December.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely planted in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words agape (love) and anthos (flower), and it has become invasive in parts of Australia and New Zealand.
